issues.detail: The Greek 'ταρταρωσας' (Tartarus) is a specific proper noun for a place of punishment, but the Vietnamese 'nơi tối tăm' (dark place) is a descriptive translation that loses the specific identity of the location. However, per instructions not to flag proper names unless it changes the claim, I will look at 'παρεδωκεν εις κρισιν τετηρημενους'. The Greek 'τετηρημενους' refers to the angels who were kept/preserved (the ones who remained), but the Vietnamese 'để giữ lại' suggests a purpose (in order to keep), which changes the grammatical function of the participle from a description of the subjects to a goal of the action.

The Greek 'τετηρημενους' is a masculine plural nominative participle describing the angels. The Vietnamese 'để giữ lại' translates this as an infinitive/purpose clause, changing the meaning from 'the kept ones' to 'in order to keep'.
